description: Day-to-day problems with the volume, fragmentation and follow-through of email, chat messages, notifications and contacts across personal and work life.

items.title: Reply-all clutter on group emails
items.problem: People hit reply-all on messages that only concern the sender, so everyone's inbox fills with 'thanks' and 'noted' replies that have to be opened and deleted.
items.who: office workers on large distribution lists
items.workaround: manually delete, mute the thread, or set up filters
items.source_quote: Almost a third (29 percent) said being copied on the 'reply all' function was the most irksome email practice.

items.title: Reply-all 'remove me' storms
items.problem: One accidental mass email triggers a chain of 'take me off this list' replies, each going to the whole list, generating dozens of junk emails in an hour.
items.who: anyone on a company- or organisation-wide mailing list
items.workaround: delete them all, mute thread if the client supports it
items.source_quote: waking up to numerous emails saying 'Take me off your list,' 'Me too,' and 'Remove me' - all sent with reply all

items.title: Overly long emails and huge attachments
items.problem: Colleagues send rambling messages and large unsolicited files, so figuring out what is actually being asked takes several reads and the mailbox fills up.
items.workaround: skim, ask the sender to summarise, or ignore
items.source_quote: receiving large, unsolicited files (cited by 29 percent) and messages that are too long (cited by 16 percent)

items.title: Email eats a third of the workweek
items.problem: The average professional receives over a hundred emails a day and spends hours each week just sorting, reading and triaging them rather than doing real work.
items.workaround: filters, inbox-zero routines, checking email in batches
items.source_quote: The average professional receives 117 emails daily while spending nearly 28 percent of their workweek just managing their inbox

items.title: Email volume keeps climbing each year
items.problem: Even after unsubscribing and filtering, the amount of email arriving grows year over year, so any system set up last year is already overwhelmed.
items.workaround: periodic mass unsubscribe sessions, declaring email bankruptcy
items.source_quote: 73% of respondents indicate their email volume has grown over the past 12 months.

items.title: Checking email long after work ends
items.problem: The inbox never resolves, so people keep compulsively checking it in the evening and on weekends and feel drained by an unfinished pile.
items.workaround: remove the mail app from the phone, set do-not-disturb schedules
items.source_quote: the flat, depleted feeling of facing an inbox that never resolves, and the checking habit that follows you out of work hours

items.title: Tracking emails still awaiting a reply
items.problem: After sending a question or request, there is no reliable way to see which of your sent emails have gone unanswered and need chasing.
items.who: anyone coordinating work or services over email
items.workaround: manual 'Pending' folders, flags, spreadsheets, or memory
items.source_quote: making your Outlook a virtual 3-basket system by adding a 'Pending' folder

items.title: Hundreds of unread messages pile up
items.problem: Unread counts on email and texts climb into the hundreds, and once past a certain point the backlog feels impossible to ever work through.
items.who: busy people, students, people with ADHD
items.workaround: ignore the badge, mark all as read, declare bankruptcy
items.source_quote: People who have 500+ unread text messages or emails, how? Why?

items.title: Reading a text and forgetting to reply
items.problem: A message is opened when there is no time to answer, the notification disappears, and the person is unintentionally ghosted for days.
items.workaround: mark as unread, pin the conversation, leave notifications unopened
items.source_quote: read a text message and leave it as unread, so when you return to the app with more time to reply, you're reminded

items.title: Long multi-question texts feel like tasks
items.problem: A message with several questions or one that needs a thoughtful answer gets mentally filed as a big job to do later, and later never comes.
items.workaround: reply with a placeholder, or avoid it entirely
items.source_quote: categorized as 'big tasks, to be completed after I have finished the thing.'

items.title: 'I'll reply later' never happens
items.problem: Time blindness means the intention to answer later evaporates, and the message resurfaces a week later when it is embarrassing to respond.
items.workaround: draft now and schedule send, set phone reminders
items.source_quote: time blindness, making 'I'll reply later' a total lie

items.title: Anxiety over wording a reply
items.problem: Composing even a short answer stalls on worries about tone and saying the wrong thing, so the reply is delayed or never sent.
items.who: people with social anxiety or ADHD
items.workaround: draft in notes, ask a friend to check, overthink and delay
items.source_quote: 'What if I say the wrong thing?', 'I don't have the energy to reply right now,' 'They'll think I'm mad'

items.title: Ghosting people in 50+ work chats
items.problem: With dozens of active Slack conversations and constant tagging, it is impossible to keep track of who asked what, so many messages simply go unanswered.
items.who: employees at large companies using Slack or Teams
items.workaround: save messages for later, accept ghosting, mute channels
items.source_quote: 50+ work-related Slack conversations and groups with constant tagging makes it impossible to keep track and respond to everyone

items.title: Not knowing which channel a message will arrive on
items.problem: A colleague may answer by email, Slack, Teams or text regardless of the stated preference, so people waste time hunting across apps for a time-sensitive reply.
items.workaround: check every app repeatedly, ask people to use one channel
items.source_quote: uncertain whether an email, Slack message, or notification from another platform will arrive next

items.title: Can't find an earlier chat discussion
items.problem: Decisions and details buried in threads and channels are almost impossible to locate again, so people re-ask questions that were already answered.
items.workaround: scroll back, ask again, copy key points into a doc
items.source_quote: making it difficult to find or refer back to earlier discussions

items.title: Chat history expiring after 90 days
items.problem: Workspaces on free or restricted plans delete messages after a few months, so context needed to track ongoing work is silently lost.
items.who: small teams and volunteer groups on free Slack plans
items.workaround: manually copy important messages elsewhere
items.source_quote: Slack messages expire after 90 days, causing valuable information loss

items.title: No way to filter signal from noise in channels
items.problem: Important discussions get lost among memes and status chatter because there is no way to separate high-value messages from low-value ones.
items.workaround: leave channels, rely on being @-mentioned
items.source_quote: lack the ability to filter high-quality information from low-quality, causing them to miss important discussions

items.title: Interrupted every two minutes at work
items.problem: Emails, chat pings and meeting alerts arrive constantly during core hours, and each interruption costs many minutes of lost focus.
items.workaround: do-not-disturb blocks, closing chat apps, headphones
items.source_quote: The average knowledge worker is interrupted by a meeting, email, or chat every 2 minutes during core work hours.

items.title: Trivial app alerts look as urgent as family
items.problem: A game or shopping app notification looks and sounds exactly like a message from a family member, so every buzz has to be checked.
items.workaround: turn off notifications per app, custom sounds for VIPs
items.source_quote: most alerts coming from apps they barely use yet demanding attention as urgently as messages from family or critical work emails

items.title: Notification cleanup that never sticks
items.problem: People spend hours unsubscribing, muting and uninstalling, only to reinstall and resubscribe and end up back where they started.
items.who: anyone trying to tame their phone
items.workaround: phone on silent, leave it in another room, turn it off
items.source_quote: spend hours unsubscribing, deleting, uninstalling, and toggling settings, but find themselves reinstalling and resubscribing

items.title: Nearly a hundred notifications per day
items.problem: Email, chat, calendar and project-tool pings add up to roughly a hundred alerts a day, far more than can be triaged thoughtfully.
items.workaround: silence everything and check manually, risk missing things
items.source_quote: workers receive 96 daily notifications encompassing email alerts, Slack or Teams messages, calendar reminders

items.title: Phone repeatedly re-notifies old unread SMS
items.problem: The phone keeps re-alerting about the same unread text every few minutes until it is opened, even when it is spam or already handled.
items.workaround: open every message, dig through repeat-alert settings
items.source_quote: Why does Android keep repeatedly notifying me about unread SMS?

items.title: Email notifications arrive 30 minutes late
items.problem: Mail apps deliver push alerts long after the email lands, so time-sensitive messages like codes or meeting changes are seen too late.
items.workaround: manually refresh, switch mail apps
items.source_quote: Gmail notifications routinely arrive 20 to 40 minutes after the email actually lands

items.title: Email search returns random old results
items.problem: Searching the mailbox for a known message surfaces irrelevant years-old emails first, so finding a recent attachment or thread takes minutes of scrolling.
items.who: Outlook users, anyone with a large mailbox
items.workaround: guess sender and date filters, scroll manually
items.source_quote: the search function throws up totally random results including incredibly old emails at the top of the list

items.title: Combined inbox missing across accounts
items.problem: With several email accounts, the mobile client shows no working unified view, so each account has to be opened separately to see new mail.
items.who: people with work and personal accounts
items.workaround: forward accounts to one address, check each account in turn
items.source_quote: the combined inbox feature does not work in iOS, requiring users to click on individual accounts

items.title: No single inbox for all chat apps
items.problem: Messages arrive across WhatsApp, iMessage, Instagram, Slack and email, and no app truly gathers them, so people cycle through five apps to catch up.
items.who: anyone with friends and colleagues on different platforms
items.workaround: check each app in turn, partial aggregators
items.source_quote: lots of apps that claim to be universal texting apps don't truly deliver

items.title: Group chat buzzing for irrelevant messages
items.problem: A large group chat generates a notification for every message, even when most of the conversation has nothing to do with you.
items.who: members of family, school and hobby group chats
items.workaround: mute the whole group and risk missing things
items.source_quote: organize a group into subgroups so you keep what you want and mute what you don't

items.title: Only wanting alerts when mentioned
items.problem: In a group text there is no way to hear only about messages that apply to you, so it is all-or-nothing between constant pings and total silence.
items.workaround: hide alerts and rely on @-mentions where supported
items.source_quote: How to Only Get Notifications for Group Texts That Apply to You

items.title: Being @-mentioned for non-urgent things
items.problem: People tag others in group chats for trivial comments, which cuts through mutes and forces a look at something that did not need one.
items.workaround: ask people to stop, leave the chat
items.source_quote: In group chats, you must resist the temptation to @

items.title: Overwhelmed by group chat volume
items.problem: Several active group chats produce hundreds of messages a day, and catching up after a few hours away feels like homework.
items.who: people in multiple friend, family and parent groups
items.workaround: skim, mark as read without reading, leave groups
items.source_quote: 40% of respondents indicated they were overwhelmed by group chat messages and notifications

items.title: Group chat drama pushes people out
items.problem: Petty disputes and off-topic chatter make group chats stressful, and leaving means losing the useful logistics that were also shared there.
items.who: members of family and friend group chats
items.workaround: mute, leave, start a smaller side chat
items.source_quote: a widespread source of petty drama, anxiety, and annoyance, causing people to leave their chats in droves

items.title: Duplicate contacts multiplying after sync
items.problem: Syncing contacts across phone, Gmail and iCloud creates duplicates and triplicates, and deleted duplicates reappear within a week.
items.who: people using several devices or accounts
items.workaround: manual merges, third-party dedupe apps
items.source_quote: deleted contacts re-populate within a week when using iCloud syncing across multiple devices

items.title: Dedupe tools mangle contact data
items.problem: Contact-merge apps meant to fix duplicates sometimes overwrite photos and fields with the wrong person's data, making things worse.
items.who: people cleaning up their address book
items.workaround: restore from backup, fix by hand
items.source_quote: replacing most friend contacts' photos with incorrect images

items.title: Contact records incomplete and outdated
items.problem: Most saved contacts are missing fields or hold old numbers and emails, so reaching someone means guessing which entry still works.
items.who: anyone with a large address book, salespeople
items.workaround: ask mutual friends, search old chats for the current number
items.source_quote: 90% incomplete contacts, up to 74% of the records need updates, and over 25% of them are duplicates

items.title: Can't copy a name or email from a contact
items.problem: The built-in contacts app makes it awkward to copy a phone number or email to paste elsewhere, wasting time on a basic task.
items.workaround: retype it, share the contact card
items.source_quote: the inability to copy user names or other contact information such as email

items.title: Silencing the phone to cope with pings
items.problem: The only working defence against alert volume is silencing or hiding the phone, which then causes genuinely urgent calls and messages to be missed.
items.workaround: silent mode, phone in another room, emergency bypass for a few contacts
items.source_quote: overwhelming to the point where they turn their phone to silent, leave it in another room, or turn it off

items.title: Unsubscribing that never takes effect
items.problem: Promotional emails keep coming after unsubscribing, or the sender uses a slightly different list each time, so the inbox refills within days.
items.workaround: mark as spam, use alias addresses, bulk-unsubscribe tools

items.title: Scam texts and robocalls every day
items.problem: Daily spam texts and spoofed calls interrupt and make it hard to trust any message from an unknown number, including legitimate ones like delivery updates.
items.workaround: block each number, silence unknown callers, carrier filters

items.title: Text from an unknown number: who is this?
items.problem: A message arrives from a number that is not saved and gives no context, so the recipient has to awkwardly ask who it is or ignore it.
items.workaround: reverse-lookup, ask 'who is this?', search old emails

items.title: Same person, several numbers and handles
items.problem: A friend exists as an old number, a new number, a WhatsApp profile and an email, and it is unclear which one actually reaches them now.
items.who: people with international or frequently-moving friends
items.workaround: message every channel, ask mutual friends

items.title: Losing contacts when switching phones
items.problem: Contacts stored on a SIM, an old account or a different platform do not transfer cleanly to a new phone, so numbers vanish or come back without names.
items.workaround: export CSV, ask people to resend their numbers

items.title: Long voice notes that can't be played
items.problem: Friends send multi-minute voice messages that cannot be listened to in a meeting or on transit, so the reply waits until it is possible to listen.
items.workaround: play at 2x later, ask for text, ignore

items.title: Chasing people who never answered
items.problem: A contractor, landlord or colleague has not replied in a week, and there is no cue to follow up until it is suddenly urgent.
items.who: anyone waiting on others by text or email
items.workaround: calendar reminders, snooze features, sticky notes

items.title: Answering the same question repeatedly
items.problem: The same requests (address, availability, price, directions) arrive from different people every week and each one is typed out from scratch.
items.who: small business owners, landlords, parents organising events
items.workaround: copy-paste from notes, text replacement shortcuts

items.title: Deciding a date in a group chat
items.problem: Picking a dinner date with eight friends generates a hundred messages of 'I can't do Friday', and the final answer is buried and forgotten.
items.who: friend groups and families planning events
items.workaround: scheduling polls, one person takes charge and nags

items.title: Links and photos lost in chat scroll
items.problem: A restaurant link or document shared in a chat weeks ago cannot be found again without scrolling through hundreds of messages.
items.workaround: search by keyword, ask the sender to resend

items.title: Catching up after being offline a day
items.problem: Returning from a flight or a day of meetings means hundreds of messages across chats and channels with no summary of what actually needs action.
items.workaround: skim from the bottom, ask a colleague what was decided

items.title: Same alert buzzing on every device
items.problem: One message triggers the phone, watch, laptop and tablet simultaneously, and dismissing it on one device does not clear it on the others.
items.who: people with multiple Apple or Android devices
items.workaround: turn off notifications on secondary devices

items.title: Work and personal messages mixed on one phone
items.problem: Work chat and personal messages share the same notification stream, so weekend pings from work and family messages during meetings cannot be separated.
items.who: employees using personal phones for work
items.workaround: focus modes, a second phone, uninstalling work apps on Friday

items.title: Wondering whether a reply was already sent
items.problem: After juggling many threads, it is unclear whether a particular person was ever answered, leading to duplicate replies or silence.
items.workaround: re-open the thread and scroll, send a redundant reply

items.title: Drifting out of touch with friends
items.problem: Months pass without messaging a good friend because nothing prompts it, and by then reaching out feels awkward.
items.who: adults with scattered friends and family
items.workaround: birthday reminders, calendar nudges, guilt

items.title: Verification codes cluttering the SMS inbox
items.problem: One-time codes and delivery notifications fill the messaging app, so real conversations are pushed down and harder to find.
items.workaround: manually delete, auto-delete settings on some phones

items.title: Forty-reply email thread with no decision
items.problem: A long back-and-forth thread never states the final decision, so anyone joining late must read every reply to work out what was agreed.
items.who: office workers, committee and PTA members
items.workaround: ask someone to summarise, read it all

items.title: Being added to groups without asking
items.problem: Strangers or acquaintances add people to group chats and broadcast lists they never wanted, and leaving is visible and feels rude.
items.workaround: privacy settings, mute and archive, leave anyway

items.title: Messaging across time zones at bad hours
items.problem: Sending a message to someone abroad wakes them at 3am or lands unread for hours, and it is easy to forget what time it is for them.
items.who: people with international friends, distributed teams
items.workaround: check world clock, schedule send

items.title: Important message hidden in a muted group
items.problem: A muted group chat is where the one genuinely important announcement (school closure, schedule change) gets posted, and it is missed.
items.workaround: unmute and suffer, rely on a friend to relay

items.title: Dates and tasks buried in messages
items.problem: Appointments, addresses and to-dos arrive inside chat messages and emails and must be manually copied into a calendar or task list, which often does not happen.
items.workaround: screenshots, retyping into calendar, scrolling back later

items.title: Tedious per-app notification settings
items.problem: Taming alerts requires opening dozens of apps one by one and adjusting each app's own settings, so most people never finish.
items.workaround: do it once for the worst offenders, give up on the rest
